entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 13 Zec 13:1-9 . Cleansing of the Jews from Sin; Abolition of Idolatry; the Shepherd Smitten; the People of the Land Cut Off, except a Third Part Refined by Trials. 1. Connected with the close of the twelfth chapter. The mourning penitents are here comforted. fountain opened-- It has been long opened, but then first it shall be so "to the house of David," &c. (representing all Israel) after their long and weary wanderings. Like Hagar in the wilderness they remain ignorant of the refreshment near them, until God "opens their eyes" ( Ge 21:19 ) [Moore]. It is not the fountain, but their eyes that need to be opened. It shall be a "fountain" ever flowing; not a laver needing constantly to be replenished with water, such as stood between the tabernacle and altar ( Ex 30:18 ). for sin ... uncleanness-- that is, judicial guilt and moral impurity. Thus justification and sanctification are implied in this verse as both flowing from the blood of Christ, not from ceremonial sacrifices ( 1Co 1:30 ; He 9:13 , 14 ; 1Jo 1:7 ; compare Eze 36:25 ). Sin in Hebrew is literally a missing the mark or way.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13184"/><div sID="gen24880" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13184"/>2. Consequences of pardon; not indolence, but the extirpation of sin.<div eID="gen24880" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24881" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">names of ... idols--</hi>Their very names were not to be mentioned; thus the Jews, instead of Mephibaal, said Mephibosheth (Bosheth meaning a contemptible thing) (<reference osisRef="Exod.23.13">Ex 23:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.12.3">De 12:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.16.4">Psa 16:4</reference>).<div eID="gen24881" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24882" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">out of the land--</hi>Judea's two great sins, idolatry and false prophecy, have long since ceased. But these are types of all sin (for example, covetousness, <reference osisRef="Eph.5.5">Ep 5:5</reference>, a besetting sin of the Jews now). Idolatry, combined with the "spirit" of "Satan," is again to be incarnated in "the man of sin," who is to arise in Judea (<reference osisRef="2Thess.2.3-2Thess.2.12">2Th 2:3-12</reference>), and is to be "consumed with the Spirit of the Lord's mouth." Compare as to Antichrist's papal precursor, "seducing spirits ... doctrines of devils," &c., <reference osisRef="1Tim.4.1-1Tim.4.3">1Ti 4:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Pet.2.1">2Pe 2:1</reference>.<div eID="gen24882" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24883" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the unclean spirit--</hi>Hebrew, spirit of uncleanness (compare <reference osisRef="Rev.16.13">Re 16:13</reference>); opposed to "the Spirit of holiness" (<reference osisRef="Rom.1.4">Ro 1:4</reference>), "spirit of error" (<reference osisRef="1John.4.6">1Jo 4:6</reference>). One assuming to be divinely inspired, but in league with Satan. <div eID="gen24883" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13185"/><div sID="gen24884" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13185"/>3. The form of phraseology here is drawn from <reference osisRef="Deut.13.6-Deut.10.18">De 13:6-10; 18</reference>:<reference osisRef="Deut.10.20">20</reference>. The substantial truth expressed is that false prophecy shall be utterly abolished. If it were possible for it again to start up, the very parents of the false prophet would not let parental affection interfere, but would be the first to thrust him through. Love to Christ must be paramount to the tenderest of natural ties (<reference osisRef="Matt.10.37">Mt 10:37</reference>). Much as the godly love their children, they love God and His honor more. <div eID="gen24884" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13186"/><div sID="gen24885" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13186"/><hi type="bold">4. prophets ... ashamed--</hi>of the false prophecies which they have uttered in times past, and which the event has confuted.<div eID="gen24885" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24886" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rough garment--</hi>sackcloth. The badge of a prophet (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.1.8">2Ki 1:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.20.2">Is 20:2</reference>), to mark their frugality alike in food and attire (<reference osisRef="Matt.3.4">Mt 3:4</reference>); also, to be consonant to the mournful warnings which they delivered. It is not the dress that is here condemned, but the purpose for which it was worn, namely, to conceal wolves under sheep's clothing [Calvin]. The monkish hair-shirt of Popery, worn to inspire the multitude with the impression of superior sanctity, shall be then cast aside. <div eID="gen24886" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13187"/><div sID="gen24887" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13187"/>5-6. The detection of one of the false prophets dramatically represented. He is seized by some zealous vindicator of the law, and in fear cries out, "I am no prophet."<div eID="gen24887" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24888" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">man--</hi>that is, one.<div eID="gen24888" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24889" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">taught me to keep cattle--</hi>As "keeping cattle" is not the same as to be "an husbandman," translate rather, "Has used (or 'appropriated') me as a servant," namely, in husbandry [Maurer]. However, husbandry and keeping cattle might be regarded as jointly the occupation of the person questioned: then <reference osisRef="Amos.7.14">Am 7:14</reference>, "herdman," will accord with English Version. A Hebrew kindred word means "cattle." Both occupations, the respondent replies, are inconsistent with my being a "prophet." <div eID="gen24889" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13189"/><div sID="gen24892" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13189"/>7. Expounded by Christ as referring to Himself (<reference osisRef="Matt.26.31">Mt 26:31</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.26.32">32</reference>). Thus it is a resumption of the prophecy of His betrayal (<reference osisRef="Zech.11.4">Zec 11:4</reference>, 10, 13, 14), and the subsequent punishment of the Jews. It explains the mystery why He, who came to be a blessing, was cut off while bestowing the blessing. God regards sin in such a fearful light that He spared not His own co-equal Son in the one Godhead, when that Son bore the sinner's guilt.<div eID="gen24892" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24893" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Awake--</hi>Compare a similar address to the sword of justice personified (<reference osisRef="Jer.46.6">Jr 46:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.46.7">7</reference>). For "smite" (imperative), <reference osisRef="Matt.26.31">Mt 26:31</reference> has "I will smite." The act of the sword, it is thus implied, is God's act. So the prophecy in <reference osisRef="Isa.6.9">Is 6:9</reference>, "Hear ye," is imperative; the fulfilment as declared by Jesus is future (<reference osisRef="Matt.13.14">Mt 13:14</reference>), "ye shall hear."<div eID="gen24893" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24894" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sword--</hi>the symbol of judicial power, the highest exercise of which is to take away the life of the condemned (<reference osisRef="Ps.17.13">Psa 17:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.13.4">Ro 13:4</reference>). Not merely a show, or expression, of justice (as Socinians think) is distinctly implied here, but an actual execution of it on Messiah the shepherd, the substitute for the sheep, by God as judge. Yet God in this shows His love as gloriously as His justice. For God calls Messiah "My shepherd," that is, provided (<reference osisRef="Rev.13.8">Re 13:8</reference>) for sinners by My love to them, and ever the object of My love, though judicially smitten (<reference osisRef="Isa.53.4">Is 53:4</reference>) for their sins (<reference osisRef="Isa.42.1">Is 42:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.59.16">59:16</reference>).<div eID="gen24894" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24895" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">man that is my fellow--</hi>literally, "the man of my union." The Hebrew for "man" is "a mighty man," one peculiarly man in his noblest ideal. "My fellow," that is, "my associate." "My equal" ([De Wette]; a remarkable admission from a Rationalist). "My nearest kinsman" [Hengstenberg], (<reference osisRef="John.10.30">Joh 10:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.14.10">14:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="John.14.11">11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Phil.2.6">Php 2:6</reference>).<div eID="gen24895" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24896" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sheep shall be scattered--</hi>The scattering of Christ's disciples on His apprehension was the partial fulfilment (<reference osisRef="Matt.26.31">Mt 26:31</reference>), a pledge of the dispersion of the Jewish nation (once the Lord's sheep, <reference osisRef="Ps.100.3">Psa 100:3</reference>) consequent on their crucifixion of Him. The Jews, though "scattered," are still the Lord's "sheep," awaiting their being "gathered" by Him (<reference osisRef="Isa.40.9">Is 40:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.40.11">11</reference>).<div eID="gen24896" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24897" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I will turn ... hand upon ... little ones--</hi>that is, I will interpose in favor of (compare the phrase in a good sense, <reference osisRef="Isa.1.25">Is 1:25</reference>) "the little ones," namely, the humble followers of Christ from the Jewish Church, despised by the world: "the poor of the flock" (<reference osisRef="Zech.11.7">Zec 11:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.11.11">11</reference>); comforted after His crucifixion at the resurrection (<reference osisRef="John.20.17-John.20.20">Joh 20:17-20</reference>); saved again by a special interposition from the destruction of Jerusalem, having retired to Pella when Cestius Gallus so unaccountably withdrew from Jerusalem. Ever since there has been a Jewish "remnant" of "the little ones ... according to the election of grace." The hand of Jehovah was laid in wrath on the Shepherd that His hand might be turned in grace upon the little ones. <div eID="gen24897" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13190"/><div sID="gen24898" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13190"/>8-9. Two-thirds of the Jewish nation were to perish in the Roman wars, and a third to survive. Probably from the context (<reference osisRef="Zech.14.2-Zech.14.9">Zec 14:2-9</reference>), which has never yet been fulfilled, the destruction of the two-thirds (literally, "the proportion of two," or "portion of two") and the saving of the remnant, the one-third, are still future, and to be fulfilled under Antichrist. <div eID="gen24898" type="x-p"/>
